# GEO report: atlas-roadmaps **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 13.08 ÷ 23 × 100 = 57. High = (13.08 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 57. A cap applies. Your robots.txt blocks Bingbot from the whole site, which goes against your declared policy of allowing AI search crawlers, so the score can't go above 40. Most of the plumbing is sound. The score is held down by one robots.txt block and a few smaller gaps. Nothing is unknown here. Everything was read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Remove the Bingbot block from robots.txt - **Why it matters:** Bing's crawler is told to stay out of the entire site. Bing's index feeds several AI search tools, and your own config says search crawlers should be allowed. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:5-6` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: Bingbot` / `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 83/100. It recovers GEO-009 (+3) and GEO-014 (+3) and lifts the cap. ### 2. Point robots.txt at your sitemap - **Why it matters:** `public/sitemap.xml` exists, but robots.txt never mentions it, so crawlers have no declared way to find it. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-9` - **What the code says:** the file has no `Sitemap:` line. Add `Sitemap: https://atlasroadmaps.example/sitemap.xml`. - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 40 on its own, because the cap stays until item 1 is done. With item 1 as well, 92. ### 3. Put the changelog text in the server HTML - **Why it matters:** The entries load in the browser after the page arrives, so crawlers that don't run scripts see an empty list. - **Where:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5` - **What the code says:** `useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/changelog').then((r) => r.json()).then(setEntries); }, []);` - **Size:** Medium (use a Remix `loader`) - **Score after this:** 40 on its own (cap). With item 1 as well, 86. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and small | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, plain valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have intended access | Problem | `public/robots.txt:5-6` blocks Bingbot site-wide. GPTBot block (line 8-9) is a training choice, not counted | | GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | Bingbot blocked on all 4 sampled routes (`public/robots.txt:6`). No noindex on public pages. `/dashboard` noindex is deliberate | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical | Problem | 3 of 4 routes clear. `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` has no `meta` and no canonical | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | 3 of 4 routes clear. `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5` | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | `app/root.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. Every route has a title and description, though pricing only inherits the generic root ones | | GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Problem | 2 of 3 routes clear. `/features` has no ``: `app/routes/_index.tsx:9` and `app/root.tsx:7` | | GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` found | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read `root.tsx` and all 5 route files. No images, and links have text | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No app profile | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Absent. Not scored | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | None. Not scored | ## Other problems found - **Features page reachable only by click handler:** `app/routes/_index.tsx:9`: `
navigate('/features')}>See all features
`. Replace it with ``. This is also the GEO-016 finding. ## Worth considering - **Back up the integrations claim:** `app/routes/_index.tsx:8`: `Integrates with all the tools you already use.` Name the actual tools on `/features` or a new page, so the claim has something behind it. - **Pricing doesn't show any prices:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`: `Plans that grow with your team. Talk to us for a quote.` List plans and prices, or say what a quote covers. Then Product/Offer structured data could label them. - **Give pricing its own title and description:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` has no `meta`, so it falls back to `app/root.tsx:2`: `{ title: 'Atlas' }`. Add something like "Pricing | Atlas" with a real description. - **Link to Features from the nav:** `app/root.tsx:7`: `
Pricing Changelog
`. Add Features and Home. - **Add site identity data:** nothing states the site's name or URL in a machine-readable way. Organization or WebSite JSON-LD in `app/root.tsx` could use the name "Atlas" and `https://atlasroadmaps.example`. - **Add `` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-6` has no dates. The changelog has real release dates you could use. - **Add head basics:** `app/root.tsx:6`: `` sets no `charset`, `viewport` or social tags (`og:title`, `og:description`). - **Give changelog releases their own pages:** each release could have its own address instead of one list at `/changelog`. - **Make the root description more specific:** `app/root.tsx:2`: `Roadmaps your whole team can follow.` doesn't say what Atlas is or who it's for. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **`/api/changelog`:** there's no route file for it in this repo, so I can't tell what it returns or whether it works. - **Status codes and headers:** actual responses and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers set outside the repo need a live scan. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`. - The `/dashboard` noindex and Disallow, and the GPTBot block, are deliberate. They're left alone and not counted. - `atlasroadmaps.example` is the real origin, per `geo.config.json`. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
